content.thinking:
I'm checking which hit types apply to the glow target and noting how textured parts need flat-color materials per texture tint. Now I'm setting up the layout constants for the file, defining top positions and border thickness before writing the full structure.

Working through the geometry for boards, side panels, back panel, and gold fascia trim, calculating box dimensions and center positions in x, y, z for each piece based on the inner width, back face, and shelf front offsets.

Still writing plinth and cornice dimensions...

I'm placing shoulder tops at y=2.18, then setting up the gable with an ogee profile sitting on top of the cornice, with gold trim along its front edge. For the columns, I'm positioning two at x=±0.745, z=0.215, starting with a lathe-turned plinth base.

Now I'm defining the full column profile: base block up to 0.11, shaft spanning 0.20–1.98 as a slightly twisted ellipse, and a lathed capital from 1.98–2.10. I'm adjusting so the shaft actually stops at 2.02 with the capital running 2.02–2.14, then adding a finial rising above 2.18 to finish the column crown.

Cornice spans ±0.85. For the twisted shaft, I'm building a vertical sweep path from 0.20 to 2.02 with tapering radius and twelve sides for smoother rings.

Now I'm designing the paint logic for spiral gold stripes against an indigo base, computing stripe placement from the twist angle and vertical position, then wrapping it in a cel shader so the gold sections get proper shadow treatment while nested paint calls still resolve correctly using the outer stripe context.

Next I'm working out the valance's scalloped outline geometry: defining the top edge, then building nine evenly spaced scallops along the bottom with control points to shape each concave arc and sharp tips between them.

I also want to check the valance's position doesn't collide with the column radius, so I'm narrowing its half-width to fit between the columns, settling on eight scallops instead, and placing the valance's front face at the right z-depth near the books.

For painting, I'm giving the valance a violet base with a gold top band and considering small gold accent dots. Then I'm placing fringe tassel cards at each scallop's bottom midpoint, oriented and sized appropriately.

For the hanging cards, I'm using a flow orientation facing upward with a 180-degree lean so they drape naturally. I'm also adding long gold tassels hanging in front of each column's capital, positioning them relative to the column shaft radius and capital size so they sit clear of the stone.

For the gable, I'm placing a sigil texture plane slightly offset from the front face, then sweeping a gold trim along the gable's outline polyline just above the bevel, using a catmull curve so the sharp peak rounds slightly while still tracking the edge geometry closely.

I'm adding crocket spikes along each side of the gable, computing outward normals from neighboring edge points so the small cones angle away from the surface correctly, mirrored for both sides. On top I'm placing a gold finial spire with a glowing aqua crescent moon topper, bringing the overall peak height to about 2.70.

For the gable's sigil, I'm working out a crescent moon emblem by building an outer arc and an offset inner circle so the two curves combine into a crescent outline without self-intersecting.

The crescent shape is the outer circle minus the shifted inner circle, leaving a left sliver: its boundary combines the left portion of the outer arc with the left-facing arc of the inner circle connecting the same two intersection points, so I'm working out the parametrization that traces both arcs continuously.

With the sweep angle resolved, the crescent traces outward counterclockwise then inward clockwise to form a valid simple polygon, with sharp endpoints marked. I'm now sketching a five-pointed star outline helper with alternating radii, then positioning a sigil circle on the gable's center plane near the peak thickness region.

Checking the gable edge heights at the ring position confirms the sigil fits within bounds, and I add small decorative stars along the gable flanks after verifying their positions stay inside the gable silhouette. Now moving on to building the flame generator and other code — starting the book system next.

Setting up book geometry data...

Still working out the pivot geometry...

Still working out book geometry placement...

For each book, I'm assembling spine and plate boxes positioned relative to thickness, then grouping them by cover color so all geometries of the same color get merged and painted together with a mottled, slightly darkened cel shader. Next I'm moving on to generating the pages geometry.

Setting up cover colors and tints...

Writing the row-generation logic for shelf placement...

Still planning tier layout...

For the stacked tomes, I'm working out sizes and positions so the top book lands around 0.345, then placing a small candle with holder and flame on top, keeping its total height under the 0.50 ceiling—tight fit, so I'll shrink the candle to 0.06 tall. The uppermost tome also needs the hero treatment with an emblem, gem, and clasp.

I'm adding emblem decals across all three books plus a glowing aqua gem with gold setting at the top book's center, and gold corner protectors on the top book computed by rotating local corner offsets into world space using the yaw angle. I'll skip strap/buckle details for the stacked set and just keep the corner gems for now.

For tier 1, I'm placing a row of leaning books with a crescent-moon bookend plate (gold with crescent glow cutout) near the right side to prop them up, plus a crystal ball on a stand nearby.

Checking the hourglass top clears the shelf ceiling with room to spare, then for the right section I'm placing three potion bottles of varying heights directly on the shelf with cork stoppers, spaced across the remaining width, leaving extra room for a small row of tiny standing books.

For the next tier up, I'm laying out a scroll rack with slatted frame and cells on the left, standing books filling the middle, and an armillary sphere on the right—working out stand height and ring radius so the rings' top clears the shelf ceiling with a small margin.

Moving to the next shelf, I'm placing an open glowing tome on a slanted A-frame lectern, adding a candle in a holder nearby, lining up more standing books on the right, and hanging a small star-shaped charm down from the shelf above.

Separating the crystal in depth from the star avoids overlap. For T4, I'm laying out tall slim grimoires on the left, a small three-candle stand centered, and an amber sun orb on the right with a few short books nearby, checking each item's radius against its neighbors for clearance. Moving up to the shoulders row, I'm starting with a large candelabra on the left side.

The gable's slope is nearly flat out near x=0.5, so I need to narrow its base width to around 0.46 to free up enough room for items on the shoulders at roughly x=±0.58, since otherwise the slab base would overlap with them.

I'm checking the finial, sigil circle, and crest heights against the new gable peak, then verifying the candelabra and hat placements don't clash—the hat's brim nearly touches the column finial, so I need to check the clearance there carefully.

Now I'm placing floor-level props on the rug: a tome pile and candle on the left, an urn with scrolls on the right, and a candle cluster centered in front, while making sure the rug's footprint comfortably contains the shelf plinth.

Writing urn lathe profile...

Adding gold stripe bands and a dotted spot motif via angle-based patterning on the lathe, then planning a fan of tilted scroll cylinders inside the urn.

Now I'm designing the scroll builder itself, giving each scroll a cream cylindrical body, spiral decal end caps, and a thin ribbon ring wrapped around its middle.

I need to orient geometry using the existing `aim()` math helper rather than Three.js's built-in quaternion methods, since those are restricted for this module. I'll build a `place(geo, at, dir?, axis?)` helper that composes the transform matrix for positioning and orienting each piece.

For the scroll rack lattice, I'm working out a diamond-pattern grid with 45° crossing lines, computing cell centers and boundaries based on the rack's x/y extents and a diagonal spacing value.

Checking boundaries, I land on 8 valid scroll positions forming a diamond pattern: two stacked vertically, two spread horizontally, and four at the diagonal corners within the rack's bounds.

Checking the diamond cells against the rack rectangle bounds, I'm finding that cells near (±1,±2) get clipped since their extents exceed the rectangle's half-height, so I'll keep only the 8 unclipped cells plus consider partial edge cases carefully.

Now I'm adding a thin vertical frame post at the rack's right edge, then working out how to clip the diagonal slat lines against the rectangle — computing for each slope direction (+1 or -1) the x-range where the line's y-value stays within the rectangle's vertical bounds, intersected with the rectangle's horizontal bounds.

I'm verifying that the diagonal line family correctly passes through the lattice corners and matches the diamond centers, then setting up each slat as a rotated box whose length and angle come from the segment's endpoints.

Working out the depth placement for the scroll bodies and cylindrical end caps so they poke slightly beyond the slat at both ends...

Now I'm varying the scroll colors with tinted cream variants grouped by hue, giving each scroll a randomly colored ribbon and a gold or red wax seal, then wrapping a tied ribbon cylinder around the scroll body oriented along its axis. I'm starting the hero orb builder function, beginning with a lathed gold base profile for its stand.

Working out the claw geometry wrapping around the sphere...

Now I'm designing the potion bottles using a lathe profile for the glass body and neck, with a separate inner lathe for the glowing liquid colored below the neck line, keeping the glass outer shell distinct from the glowing contents.

Still defining the lathe profiles...

Checking the total height against shelf clearance, the full hourglass with plates comes to .38, too tall for the .32 gap, so I'll scale it down and skip the lying books, settling on a total height of .24 with a .05 pad instead.

I'll scale the whole outline by .65 to get a .15 glass height, then move on to the armillary sphere. Writing stand and ring geometry...

Still writing geometry setup...

Now I'm planning the lectern piece: a base, post, and tilted reading-board slab angled so the surface faces upward and toward the viewer, working out the right rotation on the X axis.

For the open book on top, I'm thinking through two angled page blocks forming a V shape with covers underneath and glowing rune textures, and considering whether I need a grouping mechanism since parts only support a single transform each.

I'll compute a local-to-world matrix combining translation and rotation for the slab, then manually apply that matrix to each sub-geometry before adding it as a part. For the page texture planes, I'm working out the rotation needed so the plane normal faces upward and the texture reads correctly from the viewer's perspective.

Now I'm figuring out the tilt for the open pages: each side rotates outward around the spine axis by about 8 degrees, with the +x page rotating positively and the -x page rotating negatively, translating each page to its offset position before applying that rotation.

I'm sizing the page blocks and covers for the open book and checking the overall lectern height stays under the limit once the tilted pages are accounted for, then adding a few tiny glowing star-shaped flecks floating above the pages for atmosphere.

For the candelabra, I realize five arms across won't fit the shoulder width available, so I'm redesigning it as a narrower 3-branch triangular layout with a central candle, which fits comfortably within the space. I'm also considering whether to add a floor-level cluster of candles in front for extra visual interest.

Now I'm structuring a candle-building function that handles wax cylinders, optional brass holder dishes, wax drips, flame scaling, and lean angle, merging geometries by color where possible for efficiency. Writing candle geometry code...

Still writing flame and wax geometry...

I should double check that merging geometries with mismatched attributes won't break things, but position/normal/uv coverage looks fine across the shapes I'm using. I also need a separate bucket for textured planes since those need their own material path, and I should tally up the flat color count to stay within budget, counting tints and glow colors but not paints.

Now I'm writing out the full file, making sure there are no unused imports that would trip up typechecking. I'm generating SVG book-spine textures for the shelf...

Still writing SVG code...

Adding leaves, diamond nodes, star accents, and a border rect to the filigree, then scaling for the 1024 size. Now I'm sketching the tassel SVG with a curved cord shape at the top.

Still writing tassel details...

I'm also laying out the page-text texture with a cream background and paper-colored borders, plus planning a glowing runes texture.

Writing SVG code...

Now I'm designing a scroll-end texture with concentric rings resembling a rolled paper tip.

For the rug pattern, I'm computing a rectangular distance metric from each point to define border bands (gold trim, navy stripe, diamond lattice pattern) before transitioning into the main field region.

In the center, I'm defining an elliptical medallion with concentric gold/teal rings and a star shape computed from the angle around the center, filling the star interior gold and surrounding area teal, plus a subtle dot grid texture in the field — flat lighting on top should be enough without needing extra cel-shading.

Now I'm outlining the rug as a rounded rectangle extrusion with chamfered corners around 1.25m by 0.63m, skipping fringe details for simplicity, then planning to place lying books and a candle on top of it, and leaving things like name plaques out of scope.

I'm sketching a shading helper that scales RGB channels by a factor, then building the back panel paint with a navy gradient base blended using noise and a cell-based pattern for subtle texture variation, intending to layer twinkling stars on top.

Adding star cell logic...

Under faces get shadow automatically from the cel shading. Now I need to work out floor contact: plinth starting at y=0, rug thickness sinking slightly to blend in. Then I'm working out the hat geometry, lathing the brim and cone profile and sweeping a curved bent tip using control points for a smooth bezier curve.

Still shaping the sweep geometry... I'll smooth the tube with a tapering radius array and a point-cap at the tip, then apply a spotted paint for the texture, with stars as small circles and a gold lathe ring for the band at the cone's base.

I'll settle on radius 0.105 for the torus and add a gold buckle box up front, keeping the hat upright rather than tilting since placing parts individually makes rotation tricky. For the candelabra on the opposite side, I'm sketching out a lathe profile for its base and stem, building up the shape point by point to reach the right height.

Writing arm sweeps and cup lathes...

I'm sizing candle heights at the three cups (0.1, 0.12, 0.14) with a 0.06 flame on top, calculating the tallest point comes out around y=2.61.

Now I'm designing a floor candle cluster: a lathed tray with varying radii, a mix of pillar candles at different heights and radii, plus thin tapered candles, deciding to keep it simple and skip the lantern idea. Then I'm adding a hanging star charm on a hinge joint with a chain rod dropping to a gold extruded star and a crystal bead below it.

I'm writing a function to generate the star's outline points, alternating between outer and inner radii at angles around the circle, marking the inner points as sharp corners for the geometry tuple types.

Now I'm scaling that for a smaller 4-point sparkle shape, then setting up the extrusion thickness for these star elements. I'm turning to paint definitions next, setting up a mottled indigo cel shader for the gable face and lacquer frame, then starting on a wood grain paint for the boards.

Setting up the file structure...

Writing geometry helper constants...

Setting up gather functions...

Writing book geometry code...

Adjusting the pages box depth so it sits flush against the spine plate without gaps, tweaking the z-offset slightly to close a tiny 0.002 gap.

Skipping top/bottom caps since cover plates are thin enough already. For decals, I'm placing the spine texture plane just outside the spine plate's z-position and adding an optional top emblem plane rotated to face outward, verifying the rotation produces the correct outward normal direction.

I'm also checking lying-down book orientation: after a -90° Z rotation, the local up axis maps correctly to world up, and after the -90° Y rotation for the top decal, the plane's local width axis maps onto world +Z, keeping the texture orientation consistent. Now I'm starting to write the function that positions standing books, computing center coordinates and handling optional leaning by adjusting pivot points.

Writing standing book logic...

Placing small gold corner protectors...

I'm orienting the torus ring along the local x-axis for the gold trim, and planning to include spine decals for standing hero grimoires too. Now I'm sketching out a scroll-building function that takes direction, length, radius, paper and ribbon materials, and flags for knobs and end decals, so I can generate the body geometry consistently.

Writing scroll geometry...

I'll use mottled texture for parchment and move on to composing the rack, urn, and floor scrolls. For urn scrolls I'm computing tilted directions and positioning the base inside the urn opening, while the floor pile stacks books with randomized yaw and a candle resting at the top of the stack.

Counting up all the SVG texture elements needed (spines, sigil, filigree, tassel, orb, runes, page text) comes to around 14 textures total, and I need to check whether these fit into a 4096×4096 atlas or if some tiles will need to shrink -- might be safer to drop the paint size to 1024 to avoid overflow.

Deciding on 1024 as the texel resolution gives roughly 5.8mm detail across the ~25m² painted area, which should be fine for spine decals even if not hyper-detailed; I'll start there and bump to 2048 if the atlas has room. Now writing the orb texture function that builds a radial gradient SVG with highlight and shadow colors.

Still writing SVG code...

Now I need to plan the joint hierarchy carefully: root plus the two armillary rings, the charm, and possibly additional links.

Working out the armillary sphere geometry now — center position, ring radii, and how the meridian and equator rings attach via separate joints for rotation.

Still planning joint and geometry setup...

I'm checking orb placements on tracks: for V1 near T0, computing sphere center height from stand offset and radius so the top stays under 0.50, confirming .09 radius fits with top around 0.38. For V2 on T4, verifying a .075 radius orb tops out near 1.95, safely under the 2.10 ceiling, while considering whether a slightly larger radius still fits.

Now I'm sketching out the file structure before writing it: sections for imports/palette/textures, builder helpers, the overall structure, book tiers, props, floor, and final flush. I'm also working out a gable profile using an ogee curve function to generate the roofline points from base to peak, mapping parameter t from the right base corner up to the peak coordinates.

Checking the derivative to confirm the ogee curve rises monotonically from base to peak. I'm constructing the full outline polygon by mirroring the right-side points to build the left side, running up to the sharp peak, then back down the right side to close the shape, treating the base corners as sharp points for the geometry.

Now I'm setting up the extrusion call with placement, thickness, and bevel, then planning the gold trim path along the edges using a Catmull curve to smooth the ogee knots while keeping the peak sharp, and figuring out how to position cone-shaped crockets along each edge point using tangent-based normal estimates.

Still placing cone gold and shaping the gable finial lathe profile for the peak...

Checking the sigil geometry against the ogee curve confirms it clears the threshold, so that constraint holds. Now I'm setting up the side-panel texture decals as outward-facing planes positioned just outside the body surface.

I'll place the decal centered at z 0 spanning .30 width and 1.8 height, skip gold inlay lines and plaque text for now, and keep the same paint on front and back of the rear panel. I'm deciding to skip optional spiral corbel scrolls on the gable flanks for later, and move on to writing the file with tassel-textured valance cards and frame definitions for the card elements.

Working through the hanging orientation now: since cards face along the flow direction and the doc notes they appear upside-down when seen from downstream, I need to actually draw the tassel artwork inverted -- knot at the SVG-bottom, fringe at the SVG-top -- so that when hung, it renders correctly with the root at the attachment point.

I'll define the loop, cap, and skirt regions in screen-space coordinates, then wrap the drawing in a group with a flip transform so it renders right-side up without reworking the math. Same approach applies to any other hanging card element, and the plane geometry's UV orientation should be fine as-is.

Now I'm writing out the full code, starting with a row-generation function and a palette of anime-style cover colors, choosing gold or silver tint accents based on how light or dark each cover color is.

Still working through placement details: checking the rug's position relative to the shelf plinth, setting floor-level items at a base height of 0.02, and deciding against adding extra decorative elements like floating quills before finalizing the write.

input.command: ls scratch/wizardBookshelf; sed -n 1,60p scripts/typecheck.ts | head -40; grep -n "OutlineInput" src/builder.ts | head -3; grep -n "export type SweepOptions" -A6 src/sweep.ts | head -12
